panels.content:
1- Text Tagging:

Using all the information from the previous definition, we are now able to tag geometric members with Text for Digital Fabrication.

We will be using some of the following components:

- "Item Index" provides the index of a certain item in a List.
This is a useful component for numbering.
For example, the first Panel of a List has the index "0", and so it could be numbered as "Panel 0".
- "Concatenate" concatenates fragments of Text

- Grasshopper provides sometimes values with many decimal places (in this case, the areas have 6 decimal places).
In order to solve this, we can use the "Expression" component in order to round the values.

Bring a new "Expression" component and double-click on it, then paste the following expression:
Round(number, decimals)

Make sure to rename the inputs with "number" and "decimals".

Connect the values with the number input.
Indicate the desired decimal place with an integer to the "decimals" input.
The output will then give the desired rounded values.

- "Text Tag 3D": Represents 3D text tags.

2- Dimensioning:

One of Grasshopper's most powerful tools is dimensioning. Having the geometry, we are now able to choose specific elements and dimension them parametrically.

In this case, the process is very simple:
1- We need to dimension the triangles in the square grid.
2- Therefore, we need to find their edges (this is the element of each triangle to be dimensioned)
3- "Deconstruct Brep" provides all edges.
4- "Curve Length" provies all curve lengths.
Using the previously found Function that reduces the decimal places, we can control the numbers.
5- "End Points" provides all curves end points, snapping the dimension lines.
6- "Aligned Dimension" is the main component generating the dimensions.
7- Check the other dimension components under the Tabs
"Display" > "Dimensions"

5- Orienting & Flattening (for Digital Fabrication): 

- Build a new Surface in Rhino and give it a sharp curvature by manipulating the control points.

- Use the "Mesh Surface" component.

- Triangulate all meshes.

- Convert all meshes into Surfaces.

- Make a "Square Grid" in order to use the grid cells as targets for the oriented and flatenned surfaces.

- We will check several ways of orienting and flatenning surfaces in 3D, from being placed on a geometry to being placed flat on XY plane.

3- Weaving:

One of Grasshopper's interesting components is "Weave".

Let's check it out with a practical example below:

1- Build a Square Grid of points.

2- Make a series of Culls with following booleans as per the example:
True
False

&

False
True

3- Move in the Z direction the specific points and weave the highered points with the other points.

4- Interpolate the weaved points to make curves.

5- Apply a final Cull pattern to the interpolated curves.

6- Optional: Move one set of the culled curves in Z direction.

7- Pipe all curves.

True
False

False
True

Weaving lets you alternate while choosing elements from different Lists, following a set pattern: In this case, the "Weave" component is choosing 1st item from List 0, then 1st item from List 1, then 2nd item from List 0, then 2nd item from List 1, etc...

IMPORTANT: 
If you zoom in on the component, "plus" & "minus" signs that let you add/remove more Lists to weave together, following any chosen pattern set in P INPUT.

False
True

When we want to manipulate the Mesh Faces, the "Deconstruct Mesh" component is not useful to choose the Faces >> List item does NOT work!

However, we can use "Face Boundaries" component and then convert them to NURBS by using "Boundary Surfaces"! We are now able to choose the Faces!
Double click to edit panel content…
Double click to edit panel content…
We also sort the planes so that they are in the same order as their respective surfaces

1- Orienting:
- Use "Orient" component.
- Feed the new Surfaces into the G INPUT.
- Evaluate all surfaces and use the Frames OUTPUT from the Evaluate Surface as INPUT A in the "Orient" component.
- Get the center of all grid cells from the Square Grid andfeed them in the INPUT B of "Orient" as the target planes.
- Result: All surfaces are oriented onto the XY Plane and placed inside the Square Grid.
However, the oriented surfaces are not ordered according to their sizes, and it looks like all cells have been filled, while there are less surfaces on the original geometry than the number of cells.
So, let's try to solve these issues...

2- Sorting:
- Sort all surfaces according to their areas.

3- Short Listing:
- Use the "Short List" component to get rid of additional cells from the Square Grid by using the shortest list length.

4- Orient Direction:
- Try the "Orient Direction" component and see the difference.
- It looks like all surfaces are rotated randomly. Although this did not happen with the previously used components, let us try to solve this issue.

5- Orienting each surface alone by its geoemtric properties: Longest side to be along X axis:
- Get the Edges of the Geometry from previous component "Orient Direction" using the "Brep Edges" component.
- Get the Length of all curves using the "Curve Length" component.
- Sort all Curve Lengths using the "Sort List" component.
- Reverse the A OUTPUT (so that the List starts with the greatest values of Curve Lenghts).
- Extract the Start & End Points of each longest edge using the "End Points" component.
- Construct 2Point Vectors based on the direction of Curves: From Start Point to End Point Direction.
- Extract the Middle Point of each Greatest Curve so that it can be used as the Reference Point when Orienting again.
- Prepare Target Direction Vectors (in X Direction) at the Centroids of the Square Grid Cells.
- IMPORTANT: Match the new Vectors Lengths at the Centroids of the Square Grid with the Vectors made by the Curves: Use an "Amplitude" component.

Alternative method:
Orienting surfaces, evaluating the oriented surfaces and using their respective frames
